summary: An early multi-target CuzBro session that established three very different summer targets: a globular cluster, a color-rich double star, and a planetary nebula.
notes: The session was part of the first serious run of smartphone deep-sky captures. Rather than treating the night as a polished imaging program, the goal was to find targets, prove they could be captured, and start learning what each object demanded.
worked: Successfully captured three different object types in one session
Established M13 as a repeatable showcase target
Recorded Albireo's blue-and-gold color contrast
Captured the recognizable form of the Dumbbell Nebula
improve: Refine focus before each target
Build longer stacked integrations
Revisit the strongest targets on later nights
nextMission: Revisit M13 and the Dumbbell Nebula with a more deliberate capture workflow.

M13.result: Successful early capture of the Great Hercules Cluster.
M13.notes: The cluster was bright and immediately rewarding, establishing M13 as one of the observatory's first repeatable deep-sky targets.
M13.lesson: Return with better focus and more integration to resolve more stars while controlling the bright core.

Albireo.result: Successful color capture of the famous double star.
Albireo.notes: The blue-and-gold contrast made Albireo stand out as a strong visual and smartphone target.
Albireo.lesson: Use steadier seeing and sharper focus to separate the pair as cleanly as possible while preserving the color contrast.

Dumbbell Nebula.notes: The planetary nebula's broad dumbbell shape was recognizable and proved to be a rewarding smartphone deep-sky target.
Dumbbell Nebula.lesson: Revisit with a longer stack and compare filtered versus unfiltered captures.

summary: A dedicated lunar imaging session focused on surface texture, crater detail, and contrast along the terminator.
notes: The Moon provided a bright, forgiving target for experimenting with short exposures and phone-based capture. The result showed useful surface texture and made video stacking the obvious next step.
worked: Strong surface contrast
Visible crater and terminator detail
Short-exposure lunar capture workflow
improve: Use video stacking for sharper detail
Refine focus before recording
Capture more frames for lucky imaging
nextMission: Record a longer lunar video and stack the sharpest frames for finer surface detail.

Moon.notes: Surface texture, craters, and contrast along the terminator were clearly visible in the final image.
Moon.lesson: Move from single or short captures to video stacking so the sharpest moments of seeing can be combined.

summary: A return to M13 followed by a successful Ring Nebula capture, expanding the archive from bright clusters into compact planetary nebulae.
notes: This session continued the rapid early target survey while also beginning the process of revisiting earlier objects. M13 returned as a familiar benchmark and M57 added a tiny, high-contrast planetary nebula to the mission archive.
worked: Reacquired and captured M13
Successfully captured the Ring Nebula
Expanded the target list into Lyra
improve: Improve focus for tiny planetary nebulae
Use more total integration on repeat targets
Compare later captures against the first attempts
nextMission: Continue revisiting M13 and return to M57 with tighter focus and a more deliberate stack.

M13.notes: M13 was becoming a familiar benchmark target and offered another chance to improve the repeatability of the capture workflow.
M13.lesson: Use each M13 revisit as a focus and tracking benchmark, then compare the result against earlier sessions.

Ring Nebula.result: Successful first recorded Ring Nebula capture.
Ring Nebula.notes: M57's compact smoke-ring shape was visible, but the small target made focus and image scale especially important.
Ring Nebula.lesson: Center at lower power, nail focus on a nearby star, and then capture with enough scale to preserve the ring structure.

summary: A focused return to M27 after the first June 19 capture.
notes: The dedicated revisit turned the Dumbbell Nebula from a survey target into an improvement target. The goal was to build on the first successful capture rather than simply prove the object was visible.
worked: Successfully reacquired M27
Dedicated the session to a known target
Built on the June 19 capture experience
improve: Increase total stacked exposure time
Compare UHC-filtered and unfiltered results
Keep focus consistent through the capture
nextMission: Return to M27 with the UHC filter and a longer stacked integration.

Dumbbell Nebula.notes: The second recorded attempt provided a chance to concentrate on capture quality instead of target acquisition alone.
Dumbbell Nebula.lesson: Use a longer stack and test the UHC filter to see whether the nebula gains useful contrast without hurting the stars.

summary: A broad summer observing session combining repeat benchmark targets with the first successful Lagoon Nebula capture.
notes: M13 and M57 were revisited again while the Lagoon Nebula added a much larger emission nebula to the archive. The night highlighted how differently compact targets and wide diffuse nebulae behave through the CPC 800.
worked: Captured M13 for a third recorded session
Revisited the Ring Nebula
Successfully captured the Lagoon Nebula
Expanded the archive into bright emission nebulae
improve: Use darker sky for diffuse nebulae
Try the UHC filter on the Lagoon Nebula
Continue increasing integration on repeat targets
nextMission: Use the repeated M13 sessions to refine the workflow and revisit the Lagoon Nebula from a darker sky with the UHC filter.

M13.notes: M13 continued serving as a repeatable benchmark while the capture and processing workflow evolved.
M13.lesson: Compare the June 19, 21, and 25 results directly and identify whether focus, tracking, or integration is producing the biggest improvement.

Ring Nebula.notes: The revisit provided another chance to improve focus and scale on a very small planetary nebula.
Ring Nebula.lesson: Keep the target centered, refine focus carefully, and favor sharp data over aggressive enlargement.

Lagoon Nebula.result: Successful first recorded Lagoon Nebula capture.
Lagoon Nebula.notes: The bright summer emission nebula showed glowing structure and star-forming detail, but its wide diffuse nature is a challenging match for the CPC 800's narrow field.
Lagoon Nebula.lesson: Revisit from a darker sky with the UHC filter and keep the framing as wide as the current setup allows.

summary: A fourth recorded M13 session dedicated to refining a familiar target and judging progress across repeated attempts.
notes: By this point M13 had become the observatory's benchmark deep-sky object. The repeated sessions created a useful history for comparing focus, tracking, exposure, and processing choices.
worked: Fourth recorded M13 session
Used a familiar target as a workflow benchmark
Created a meaningful multi-session improvement history
improve: Continue protecting the bright cluster core
Resolve more outer stars with sharper focus
Increase total integration when tracking allows
nextMission: Capture M13 again with the dedicated astronomy camera and compare it directly with the June smartphone series.

M13.notes: The repeated June attempts established M13 as CuzBro Observatory's benchmark target for tracking progress in focus, capture, and processing.
M13.lesson: The next meaningful comparison should use the dedicated astronomy camera and a larger stack rather than simply repeating the same smartphone workflow.

summary: First serious deep-sky session with the ASI294MC, focused on learning the new capture and processing workflow on two challenging galaxies.
notes: M51 was much more cooperative in processing and showed recognizable spiral structure. Fireworks Galaxy was a tougher stretch and became noisy quickly, but the session helped establish a better Siril-to-AstroShader workflow and showed how much the ASI294MC can pull out of short stacked exposures.
worked: Siril stacking workflow
M51 spiral structure emerged clearly
ASI294MC sensitivity was a major improvement
GHS stretching produced a usable deep-sky result
improve: Collect more total integration time
Improve tracking stability
Reduce background noise during stretching
Begin using calibration frames
nextMission: Revisit M51 with at least 100 subs and a more controlled processing workflow, then give Fireworks Galaxy a longer dedicated integration.

M51 Whirlpool Galaxy.result: Successful first dedicated-camera capture of M51.
M51 Whirlpool Galaxy.notes: M51 was the more cooperative galaxy in processing. Recognizable spiral structure emerged from the stack and held up better during stretching.
M51 Whirlpool Galaxy.lesson: Aim for at least 100 subs, improve tracking stability, and begin using calibration frames before the next serious M51 processing pass.

Fireworks Galaxy.result: Successful but difficult first dedicated-camera capture.
Fireworks Galaxy.notes: The galaxy was present, but background noise increased quickly when the data was stretched aggressively.
Fireworks Galaxy.lesson: Give NGC 6946 a longer dedicated integration under darker conditions and use a gentler, more controlled stretch.
